_doc: AUTHORED reading of Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35 for the 1904 target (T-1842), in the T-1840 sheet-census contract (tools/sheet_census.py). Every frontage row on the sheet and every named record on its ground is assigned here exactly once. Kinds and tiers as sheet-20.json; rulings[] as sheet-28.json, settling the sheet's identity and phase questions.

reading.by: Read by eye from the deposited sheet image (1640 x 2048 px), a half-size overview and 2x crops of each Prairie block face, 2026-10-09; the 2120 rear building and the 2140 alley building at 3-4x.
reading.conventions: Sanborn colour: pink brick, yellow frame, blue stone, buff fireproof. A crossed square marks a stable. D = dwelling, F = flats. Storey figures as printed (B = basement).
reading.limits: A 1911 label is a 1911 observation (study ruling 11): garages and the auto house are backcast as stables, the medical college and the dressmakers as the houses the 1904 Blue Book lists. The Indiana and Calumet frontages of the sheet are not Prairie frontages and are not counted here. Footprints are not digitized and no dimension is claimed. The supplied 1911 sheet is the footprint layer for 1904 (docs/map-guidance.md names no change on this sheet), except 2126, which was being rebuilt in 1904. Blue Book names are OCR-derived and only say who lived at a number.

rulings.question: 2000-2100 identities
rulings.ruling: Every Prairie frontage on sheet 35 is joined to one named record or declared map-only. Seventeen named records stand on the sheet's ground and each is joined to the frontage of its printed number. Fifteen frontages have no named record (2000, 2010, 2018, 2026, 2120, 2001, 2003, 2005, 2011, 2017, 2101, 2123, 2125 and the 2127-2129 flats); each is drawn from the 1911 sheet and carries the 1904 Blue Book household at its number as a lead, not an identity. 2129 is the flats' second number and 2141 is open ground. The joins rest on the printed number, the record's recorded lifespan or 1904 listing, and the images named on each row.

rulings.question: Robbins target-date state
rulings.ruling: On 1 July 1904, 2126 is a building site, not a finished house and not the Hamill house. Robbins bought the standing Hamill house in November 1901 (Tribune); claimed a water-tax rebate on 2126 in the winter of 1903-04 (Council, January 1904), consistent with the house being emptied; the AIC building index says he razed it in 1904; and the May 1905 Inland Architect plate shows the new house complete with bare trees. No permit or progress photograph dates the month, so the working state is a reconstructed construction stage: the new house's brick shell partly raised and unroofed, on the 1911 footprint, with the alley stable standing. The May 1905 plate is the finished design, not July 1904 evidence.
rulings.replaceable_by: a 1904 building permit for 2126 Prairie or a dated progress photograph

rulings.question: The 2031-2035 row
rulings.ruling: Three attached houses of 1869 on 25-foot lots with Lemont limestone fronts (Reid nomination p. 13), all standing in 1904: Samuel A. Tolman at 2031 (Blue Book), the Otis homestead at 2033 (Tribune, February 1904) and Mrs. H. O. Stone at 2035 (Tribune, 4 February 1904). The sheet draws three stone fronts with full-height bays and one continuous block of two-storey brick buildings on the alley behind them. 2035 is a corner house with its own mixed brick and frame rear building. The row is three houses with a shared cornice line, not three identical copies.

rulings.question: The shared 2108/2110 coach house
rulings.ruling: One building, not two. The sheet draws a single two-storey brick stable across the alley end of both lots, divided on the lot line. Glessner House has Mark Kimball's coach house spanning both lots when Rees bought 2110 from him in 1888, Rees taking the south half behind a new party wall. The February 1904 to-let notice for 2108 includes a good brick barn. Build it as one envelope with a party wall: the north half is 2108's (s35-2108-rear) and the south half is 2110's (s35-2110-rear).

rulings.question: The 2120 rear label
rulings.ruling: Read at 4x on the sheet: the two-storey brick building on the alley behind 2120 is lettered "VACANT 1ST / DRESS MAKING 2ND", with a stone alley face. The register's "rear Electric Motor Repairing label" is not on this building. Both readings are 1911 uses only, and for 1904 the building is backcast as a stable/coach house.

corrects.was: 1911 commercial use only; rear Electric Motor Repairing label.
corrects.now: 1911 commercial use only; rear building lettered VACANT 1ST / DRESS MAKING 2ND (re-read 2026-10-09, T-1842; first transcribed as an Electric Motor Repairing label).

rulings.question: Wheeler-Kohn and 2018 Prairie
rulings.ruling: The study register lists the Wheeler-Kohn house (pa-2018-s.-calumet-avenue-31) with frontage-35-061 as its map control. They share a number and nothing else: the Wheeler-Kohn house is 2018 Calumet, on the far side of the alley, and frontage-35-061 is 2018 Prairie, a narrow brick house with a stone bay where the 1904 Blue Book lists the Herricks. The Prairie frontage stays map-only, and the Calumet house is not placed by this census.

rulings.question: The 2141 frontage and the unnumbered lot north of it
rulings.ruling: Both lots are open from street to alley on the 1911 sheet, with no record, image or 1904 directory entry for either. They stay open in 1904 as a backcast, not as a reading of 1904, and are not a site for a house. The build package gives them a ground surface and their boundary; anything more needs a dated source.
